name: Bering Strait
note: At its narrowest, only about 82 km separates Alaska from Russia.
description: The Bering Strait is where two continents almost touch: about eighty-five kilometres of shallow, cold sea between Siberia's Cape Dezhnyov and Alaska's Cape Prince of Wales, with the Diomede Islands — and the International Date Line — in between. During ice ages its floor stood dry as Beringia, the land bridge by which people first walked into the Americas. Semyon Dezhnyov sailed through in 1648 and Vitus Bering followed in 1728, proving the continents separate; today the strait is the Pacific gateway to the warming Arctic and its opening sea routes.
